Southington BKMB · Sub Sale

How to sell a sub

Two parts: signing up with your friends, then selling at the door. If you can knock and tap a phone, you can do this.

Part one

Signing up

Before any of this, you pick who you are selling with and which days you are out. Do it once, at home, on a laptop or a phone.

  1. 1

    Sort out your team first

    Find your friends. Three or four of you is about right — enough to cover a street, small enough that everyone gets doors.

    Agree on a team name before anyone signs up, and agree who is going to create it. Everyone has to type the same name, so pick something you can all spell.

    Tip Do this in person, in the band room, not over five separate group chats.
    Decide together

    Who is on the team — what it is called — who creates it

  2. 2

    One person creates the team

    Open the sign-up link and type your name — it finds you on the band list. Then type your team name.

    If nobody has made it yet, the app offers to create it. Tap that, and you are the first one on the team.

    Careful Only one person creates it. If two of you both create “Sub Squad”, you end up on two different teams with the same name and the totals split in half.
  3. 3

    Everyone else joins it

    Now the rest of you open the same link, type your name, and start typing the team name. It appears in the list — tap it. Do not create it again.

    You can see who else has already signed up, so you know it worked.

  4. 4

    Pick your days

    Tap the dates you can actually sell. Tap one again to un-pick it. Only pick days you know you are free — a team that is one person short on a Saturday is a street that does not get knocked.

    Keep the link Save the sign-up link somewhere you will find it — bookmark it, or text it to yourself. If something changes, that is how you come back and fix your dates.
  5. 5

    Changing your mind later

    Open the same sign-up link and type your name. It finds you and shows what you are already signed up for.

    Want more days? Tick them and sign up again. Days you already have are not in the list — that is normal, you already have them.

    Can’t do a day any more? You cannot un-tick it, because it is not in the list. Find that day in your sign-ups and press Remove This Registration.

    On the wrong team? There is a Change team button.

    Tell someone If you drop a day, tell your team. They planned a street around you being there.

Part two

Selling

Sale day. This is the bit you do at somebody’s front door, on your phone.

  1. 1

    Put the app on your phone

    Open subsales.southingtonbkmb.com/portal/ and tap Install App. Now it sits on your home screen like a real app, and it works even when your phone has no bars.

    Tip Do this at home, on wi-fi, the night before. Not on somebody's front path.
  2. 2

    Log in once

    Type your phone number and pick your team. You stay logged in all season, so you never do this at a door.

  3. 3

    Knock. Say this.

    You do not have to make anything up. There is one sentence, and it works every time.

    What you say

    “Hi! I’m with the Southington Marching Band. We’re doing our Annual Football Sub Sales fundraiser. Would you like to buy any subs or give a donation?”

  4. 4

    Type their name and address

    Start typing the house number and the address appears — tap it. That is how the driver finds them later.

    Beside the box is 📍 Use my location. Tap it and the app fills in the nearest address it knows to where you are standing — handy on a long driveway or a house with no number on it.

    Always check the number It fills in the closest address it knows about. That could be next door, or across the street. Read it back and make sure it matches the door you are at.
    Says “Location off”? Your phone is not letting the app see where you are. Type the address instead — it works exactly the same. An adult can turn location on for the site later.
    Tip Tapping the suggestion beats typing it out. A typed address can send a driver to the wrong street.
  5. 5

    Ask for their phone number

    You need it so the driver can reach them on delivery day. Type it in.

    Underneath is a tick box: Text me about this sub order. Ask them — if they say yes, tick it and they get a receipt by text straight away, with a link to their order.

    Say this too “Save that number, so our texts reach you.” Phones hide messages from numbers they don’t know. Ten seconds at the door means they actually see the delivery message.
    Careful Don’t tick it for them. If they didn’t say yes, leave it — the order goes through exactly the same, we just don’t text.
  6. 6

    Tap what they want

    Use + and − for each kind of sub. The total adds itself up at the bottom. If they want to give extra, put it in Donation.

    Just giving money? Lots of people do not want subs but still want to help. Put the amount in Donation and take their name and phone number exactly like any other order — they get a receipt by text, same as everybody else. Leave the subs at 0.
    Anonymous Donation is a last resort Only tick it if they will not give you a name. It means no name, no number and no receipt — there is nobody to send one to. Ask first.
  7. 7

    Ask how they are paying

    Three buttons at the bottom: Cash, Check and Digital. Ask which one, then tap it.

    Ask, do not guess “Cash, check, or card?” Tapping the wrong one makes the money not add up at the end of the day, and somebody has to work out why.
  8. 7A

    Cash

    Tap Cash. Nothing else to fill in. Take the money and put it straight somewhere safe — a zip pocket or the money bag, not loose in your hand.

    Count it out loud Say the amount as you take it. It stops arguments later, and it is exactly what your tally will expect from you at the end of the day.
  9. 7B

    Check

    Tap Check and a box appears for the check number. It is the short number in the top right corner — usually three or four digits. Not the long numbers along the bottom; those are the bank and account.

    You cannot skip it The number is how the club matches the check when it goes to the bank, and the app will not save without it.
  10. 7C

    Digital — paying by card

    Tap Digital and a QR code appears. Hold your phone up so they scan it with their phone. The card page opens on their phone, not yours.

    Wait with them. When it goes through, the app says so by itself and the order saves — you do nothing.

    Never hand your phone over Hold it up so they can scan. Your phone has every order you have taken on it.
    The code expires Only good for a few minutes. If they take too long, back out to Cash or Check and start again.
    Once paid, it locks A card order cannot have its subs or donation changed afterwards — the card has already been charged. Get it right before they scan.
  11. 8

    Save it, then walk away

    Check the screen says the right subs and the right total, then tap OK. That is the order done.

    Careful Never enter the same order twice. If you are not sure it saved, look in My orders first. Two orders means two deliveries and somebody pays twice.
  12. 9

    Got something wrong? Fix it, don’t redo it.

    Tapped one too many Turkeys? Spelled the street wrong? Open My orders, find it, and press Edit. Change what is wrong and save. There is a Cancel edit button too, if you opened the wrong one.

    Never take the order again A second order does not replace the first — now there are two, and the customer gets double the subs and a double charge. Always edit.
    Card orders are different If they paid by card, the subs and donation lock — their card was already charged for exactly that. You can still fix the name, address and delivery notes. Anything else, an adult sorts out.
  13. 10

    No bars? Keep going.

    The app saves the order on your phone and sends it the moment you get signal back. You will see Queued orders counting them. Nothing is lost.

  14. 11

    End of the day

    Tap EOD Tally. It shows what you sold and what money you should be holding. Hand in the cash and checks — the card ones are already paid.
